slides: Revenue isn't profit.
A busy month can still lose money. Swipe.
Busy is not the same as profitable.
Work comes in, payroll goes out, and the margin quietly disappears in between.
Know your floor before you quote.
Decide the minimum margin you will accept. If the job can't clear it, the answer is no.
Check margin weekly, not yearly.
By the time the year ends, it's too late to fix the month that hurt you.
caption:
Revenue isn't profit.

A busy month can still lose money. The gap between what comes in and what goes out is where margins quietly disappear.

Decide your minimum margin before you quote. Check it every week, not once a year.

What number do you check every Friday? 👇

slides: Cheap quotes are expensive.
The lowest price often costs the most. Swipe.
Low bids hide the real cost.
Delays, rework and idle time don't show up on the quote. They show up in your profit.
Price the whole job, not the best case.
Add time for delays and unknowns. Your estimate is a forecast, not a promise.
Win work you can profit from.
A job that barely breaks even still uses your time, your people and your energy.
caption:
Cheap quotes are expensive.
